technical_issues.where: Project Plan & Preliminary Progress — Orbit Specifics
technical_issues.issue: 'Geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km' is incorrect: GEO requires ~35,786 km altitude; a 600 km orbit is LEO and cannot keep the satellite fixed above the reef. Also GEO imaging of the reef raises resolution/latitude coverage questions unaddressed.

No quantitative mission requirements (e.g. spatial resolution, revisit time, swath) despite citing 100 m/pixel bathymetry gap; sensor feasibility (Asner's airborne imaging spectrometer) for a satellite not examined.

overall: A well-presented, well-referenced preliminary report with a clear mission concept, detailed Gantt chart and genuine progress. Weakened by a fundamental orbit error (600 km 'geostationary') and limited preliminary technical results.

feedback.summary: A well-presented, well-referenced report with a clear mission concept (GBR bleaching monitoring), explicit users, a detailed weekly Gantt chart and genuine progress including four STK tutorials. To lift your marks, fix the orbit error (600 km is not geostationary), add quantitative mission requirements, and include preliminary technical results such as orbit or coverage calculations.
next_steps: Correct the orbit section: GEO requires ~35,786 km altitude; a 600 km orbit is LEO and cannot keep the satellite fixed above the reef. Re-examine whether GEO imaging suits reef resolution and latitude coverage, or justify an alternative orbit.

Add quantitative mission requirements (spatial resolution, revisit time, swath width) tied to the 100 m/pixel bathymetry gap you cite, and assess whether Asner's airborne imaging spectrometer concept is feasible from orbit.
Present preliminary technical results in your next report — e.g. an STK orbit/coverage analysis or link budget — with brief interpretation, and add contingency provisions to your Gantt chart plan.
Convert your footnote URLs into a formal, complete reference list so in-text citations and the reference list match fully.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (8/10). Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly states the purpose (near-real-time GBR bleaching monitoring), identifies marine and conservation scientists as users, and justifies the need with four literature citations (NOAA, National Geographic, Deepreef, Nature). To reach the top of the band, add formal, quantitative objectives and requirements — e.g. spatial resolution, revisit time, swath — and examine sensor feasibility for a satellite rather than an airborne platform.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (7/10). Your weekly Gantt chart with task descriptions is detailed and tied to mission stages (launch, orbit, ground, comms, EOL), with sources cited. The next level requires a robust plan with explicit provision for variations and contingencies — add buffer time, fallback tasks, and a short discussion of what you will do if a task slips or STK results force a redesign. Note the orbit-specifics task needs correcting (600 km is not GEO).
criteria.C3: Adequate (5/10). You show genuine progress: background research on Asner's Hawaii system and coral bleaching, plus STK tutorials 1–4. However, no preliminary technical results are presented — no orbit, coverage, or link calculations with interpretation. The 'geostationary orbit at 600 km' statement is a fundamental error that weakens the technical content. For the Accomplished level, include a preliminary set of results (e.g. an STK orbit/coverage run) with brief interpretation.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (8/10). Your report has a logical structure with clear headings, well-written prose, consistent formatting, and a clearly explained, labelled Gantt chart (gold/blue/red legend). Numbered citations match your listed sources. To perfect this, replace footnote URLs with a formal, complete reference list so every in-text citation maps fully to a properly formatted reference entry.
